newsitem.title: USA: Dollar soars to new 6-year high versus slumping mark.
newsitem.headline: Dollar soars to new 6-year high versus slumping mark.

text.p: The dollar Monday surged to a new six-year high against the mark, which continued to slump badly on expectations of enduring German economic weakness.
The dollar also rose against the Swiss franc, but ended little changed vs. other major currencies.
The dollar initially followed the British pound higher in European trade as the pound hit a seven-year high against the mark on a report showing a large decline in British inflation in June.
After a brief bout of profit-taking, the dollar rocketed higher again in New York trading, stopping just short of the key psychological level of 1.80 marks.
Traders cited a Bridge News service story quoting an unnamed Bundesbank official as saying the central bank would not intervene to support the mark, even though it was undervalued vs. the dollar.
"The dollar was trading at 1.7910 marks when the story came out. It went down to 1.7850 and then it snapped straight back up," said Stephen Jury, chief currency dealer at Union Bank of Switzerland.

The dollar ended higher at 1.7965 marks, up from 1.7773 late Friday, and rose to 1.4773 Swiss francs from 1.4665. The dollar edged lower to 113.96 Japanese yen from 114.00. The pound fell to $1.6876 from $1.6900. The dollar slipped to Canadian $1.3696 from C$1.3699.
The mark also fell heavily against the Italian lira, forcing the Bank of Italy to enter the market and buy the German currency to stop its decline, traders said.

There were unconfirmed rumours that other monetary authorities had also intervened to bolster the mark, traders said. "There were a number of central banks in Europe rumoured to be aggressive buyers of marks," said Bob Savage, chief dealer at Lehman Brothers.

The mark has suffered heavy losses in recent sessions amid signs that Germany may not meet the entry rules for a proposed single European currency, even as many of its traditionally weaker neighbours are strengthening their finances.
In the United States, data continue to show ample economic strength, drawing funds away from German investments, traders said.
On Monday, the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta reported its index of manufacturing activity rose in June, keeping alive expectations for higher U.S. interest rates.
The rally marked the 14th consecutive trading session in which the dollar has posted a new high vs. the mark, pointing to further gains ahead, traders said.
"The trend is clear. The dollar should continue upwards for a bit more, though it will be bumpy, as usual," said Christer Stefansson, a trader at Swedbank.
The dollar made sharp gains late Friday, breaching 1.78 marks and capping a strong week that turned many dollar sellers into buyers, traders said.
"Everything was set in place by the price action last week," Jury said.
Traders predicted the dollar would hover below 1.80 marks in coming sessions, but could move significantly higher if it breaks that technical resistance point.
"If we get through 1.80 marks, clearly we could see some more fireworks," Savage said.
